purpose: retrieve craft principles during prose drafting and revision
generate contrastive examples and hard negatives
optimize prose while preserving project-specific voice, canon, intent and protected language
prohibited_goal: Do not optimize toward copying a named author or memorizing copyrighted prose. Learn transferable craft decisions, abstract patterns, contrasts, and measurable effects.

source_rights_classes.PUBLIC_DOMAIN_FULL_TEXT: Full text may be stored and transformed when public-domain status is verified for the relevant jurisdiction/use.
source_rights_classes.LICENSED_FULL_TEXT: Full text may be stored only within documented license scope.
source_rights_classes.USER_OWNED_OR_AUTHORIZED: Full text may be stored when the user owns or has authorized use.
source_rights_classes.ANALYSIS_ONLY_NO_FULL_TEXT: Store bibliographic metadata, human-authored craft analysis, abstract technique descriptors and other permitted material; do not persist unauthorized full-text corpus content.

derived_artifact_types.CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Abstract rule with preconditions, desired effect, counterexamples, and failure modes.
derived_artifact_types.CONTRASTIVE_PAIR: Two non-gold training examples differing at one important decision boundary, with preferred result and explanation.
derived_artifact_types.TECHNIQUE_PROFILE: Vector/profile of prose characteristics independent of author identity.
derived_artifact_types.REVISION_TRANSFORM: Before/after transformation annotated by intended improvement and protected invariants.
derived_artifact_types.HARD_NEGATIVE: Plausible but inferior or misclassified example designed to separate near-neighbor concepts.
derived_artifact_types.REFERENCE_STATE: Canonical facts, timeline, character state, source support, protected language, and governing brief extracted separately from judgment.

guardrails: Never use one universal prose ideal.
Optimize relative to the project's declared genre, audience, voice and scene purpose.
Never replace authorial voice merely because a reference corpus has a different style.
Writer and evaluator roles must be logically separated.
Retain the original when the proposed revision does not clear the improvement threshold.
